CHANGELOG.html.title: Changelog | MGM Character Controller
CHANGELOG.html.summary: Changelog All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning. [0.8.0] - 2026-07-28 Removed Averaged multi-character camera framing (FollowStrategy.Average) — Removed the FollowStrategy.Average public enum member (breaking). It was declared but never functioned, so no runtime behaviour is lost; primary/first-character framing (FollowStrategy.First) is the replacement. None and First keep their ordinals (0, 1). See the upgrade guide (CAM-1, CAM-2) Added Performance characterization surface — A simulation-frequency × population cost matrix (sim rates {20, 30, 50, 60} Hz × counts {1, 100, 1 000, 10 000, 20 000, 30 000}) on the PerfSpawner Gym scene, plus a per-tick memory-allocation measurement. Both are measurement surfaces (not gates), recorded via Unity Performance Testing. Published with reference hardware in the performance manual: on the reference machine, in a shipped-representative config (Release, safety layers off), the 30 000-character simulation is ~8.6 ms/frame at 60 Hz (~4.7 ms at 30 Hz) with 0 B/tick allocation, terrain-only collision (PERF-2, PERF-5) 30 000-character frame-budget gate (PERF-4) — A PlayMode gate that asserts the 30 000-character frame against the 16.67 ms 60 fps budget, in two self-gating variants: simulation-only (headless) measured a 0.737 ms median frame, and the full loop with Entity Graphics render (-force-d3d11, URP host) measured a 9.107 ms median frame (mean 8.354, min 3.844, max 13.304, 120 frames) — under budget with every measured frame inside it. Measured on the reference machine in the shipped-representative config; the editor's default config (safety layers on) runs ~40% slower Museum Tour sample — A hands-off curated tour that auto-cycles through all 29 Behavior Showcase exhibits with looping bot input and a UI Toolkit placard. Requires the Behavior Showcase and Single Player samples to be imported first; adds no changes to the existing sample sub-scenes, prefabs, or package Runtime/ Network sample plan (DOC-1) — A reviewable planning document (Product~/network-sample-plan.md) covering sample scope, netcode approach candidates, determinism prerequisites, and acceptance criteria. Planning artifact only — no netcode sample is implemented in this release Jump-off momentum test (PLT-7) — JumpOffMomentumTests, a dedicated regression test on its own Gym scene for momentum carried when jumping off a moving platform; the behaviour was previously claimed but not covered by a test (PLT-7b) Changed Claim hygiene (DOC-2) — Removed unbacked marketing claims: "netcode-ready / deterministic client-server" and "guaranteed cross-machine determinism"; Cinemachine is described as camera-target driving (doc-snippet level), not a wired integration. The brittle "30 000 characters @ 60 fps" line is replaced by a general "highly scalable, performance-optimized DOTS crowds" positioning, backed by the published simulation cost matrix + transparent reference hardware (performance manual) rather than a single fps number Perf scene spawn capacity raised to 30 000 (PERF-1) — The PerfSpawner Gym scene's spawn patterns previously topped out near 10 000 characters; they now reach 30 000 so the characterization matrix can be reproduced end-to-end Fixed Museum bot re-arm ran in a partition Unity discarded — MuseumBotReArmSystem declared [UpdateBefore(typeof(FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup))] from a group where OrderFirst takes precedence, so Unity discarded the constraint and logged Ignoring invalid [UpdateBefore…] on every Play. The system now sits in [UpdateInGroup(typeof(SimulationSystemGroup), OrderFirst = true)] alongside the same UpdateBefore, so re-arm lands before input consumption instead of a frame late; the warning is gone Behavior Showcase scene-selector UI rendered blank in consumer projects — The sample's PanelSettings referenced a UI Toolkit runtime theme that existed only in the authoring project, so the scene-picker UIDocument rendered nothing after import. The theme now ships with the sample Perf population spawned idle — SimpleCharacterBotBakingSystem's seeding query excluded Prefab-tagged entities, so spawned bots did not locomote and the perf fixture had to drive them with a runtime write. The query now uses EntityQueryOptions.IncludePrefab; the spawned population self-locomotes Known issues Hybrid transform sync throws when an entity scene unloads (EntityGoTransformSyncSystem) — Unloading an entity scene while hybrid EntityGameObject companions are registered makes EntityGoTransformSyncSystem.GoTransformSyncJob index ComponentLookup<LocalToWorld> with entities the unload already destroyed, throwing System.ArgumentException from Burst and aborting that frame's sync job. Cause: the system's static transform registry is cleared only from EntityGameObject.OnDestroy, and that call is guarded by EntityManager.Exists(entity) — on an entity-scene unload the entities die before the GameObjects, so the guard is false exactly when unregistration is needed and the registry retains dangling entities for the lifetime of the process. Anyone streaming entity scenes in and out with hybrid GameObject-synced characters is affected. Measured rate on the Museum Tour sample, which streams continuously: 399 exceptions across a 28-minute hands-off session, and 122 of 123 console entries (~0.16/s) across a 12 min 35 s session — a log flood as well as a correctness problem, since the sync job aborts for the affected frame. There is no workaround inside the package: no setting suppresses it, and the only ways to avoid it are to not stream entity scenes at runtime or to not use the hybrid EntityGameObject sync path (a pure-ECS render path such as Entity Graphics is unaffected). This is not a 0.8.0 regression — an A/B probe measured an identical rate (~7 per 20 s of play) before and after this release's museum changes, and the defect is present in 0.7.0; the Museum Tour sample is the first shipped surface that unloads and reloads entity scenes often enough to make it routine. No automated test covers it (the EditMode suite does not exercise companion-GameObject teardown), so the release's suites are green while this surface is not console-clean. A fix is targeted at the proposed 0.8.1 patch; the defect is carded at Plan~/epics/hybrid-unload-sync-defect.md and recorded as open risk 9 in Product~/evidence/mgmcc-0.8.0-evidence.md §6 [0.7.0] - method (superseded by DIM-based template) PhysicsProfileValue on ILocomotionProfile — Moved to context; profiles no longer carry physics configuration [0.2.0] - 2025-10-05 Added Support for custom state machine - Refactored systems to enable user defined state machine Source Generator - The package now relies on source generator to create the input and state machine execution systems. State Machine Creation Menu - Added a creation menu to set up a new state machine [0.1.0] - 2025-07-02 Added Modular locomotion architecture – Introduces a clean separation of concerns by splitting player input, character physics, and the visual model into distinct entities. This design supports both player-controlled and AI-controlled characters, and scales to multiple characters or players in local multiplayer scenarios. State-driven movement system – Character locomotion is governed by a flexible state machine with distinct states (e.g. idle, grounded, jumping, falling, sliding) and smooth automatic transitions between them. Movement behavior is defined by data-driven profiles, making it easy to tune speeds and jump parameters without code changes. Physics-based character controller – Uses physics under the hood for robust movement and collisions. Characters utilize a capsule collider and can step over small obstacles up to a defined height, as well as traverse slopes up to a maximum angle before sliding down steeper inclines. The system handles gravity and falling, inherits movement from moving platforms (so characters ride platforms smoothly), and includes solid collision resolution to prevent getting stuck on edges or corners. Integrated input handling – Built-in support for player input, character movement direction is calculated relative to the camera’s orientation, and an optional “aim” input allows the character to align with the camera direction for intuitive control. Input capture uses the new input system for easily supporting multiple control devices. Camera tracking for characters – A camera target tracking system automatically follows player characters to keep them in view. Integration with the new input system and PlayerInputManager allows natural support for split screen local multiplayer.The camera target follows smoothly the position and rotation in both single-player and local multiplayer scenarios. The solution supports use of Cinemachine cameras. Animation-ready character models – Visual presentation is decoupled from logic by spawning a separate model GameObject for rendering and animation. The locomotion system keeps the model’s transform in sync with the character’s state, enabling developers to hook up animations (e.g. running, jumping) to the character’s movement without affecting the underlying physics simulation. Customizable locomotion profiles – Character movement characteristics are driven by scriptable Locomotion Profile assets. These profiles define parameters like movement speed, acceleration, turning rate, allowed jump count, jump heights, and gravity settings for each character. This allows easy tweaking of locomotion behavior and per-character tuning by adjusting profile values in the editor. Example scenes – Included sample scenes demonstrate the locomotion system in action. A single-player example and a local multiplayer example are provided, showcasing basic player movement, jumping, camera follow, and multiple characters controlled simultaneously.

Aggregates the base locomotion context, character physics profile, locomotion profile, input, and state data into a single pass-by-ref struct. MinimalInput Per-frame input data for the Minimal locomotion system. Add fields for movement direction, jump, etc. MinimalInputReaderSystem Reads player inputs from input asset instances and applies them to the input component on each controlled character entity. MinimalInputReaderSystem.ApplyInputsJob MinimalLocomotionSystem MinimalPlayerInputManagerSystem Manages the lifecycle of player input asset instances for the Minimal locomotion system. Instantiates input assets for newly spawned players and destroys them when players are removed. MinimalProfile Locomotion profile data for the Minimal state machine. Add fields to configure movement parameters. MinimalStateData Persistent per-entity state data for the Minimal state machine. Add fields for timers, counters, etc. MinimalStateMachine Generated state machine component for Minimal. Stores the current state and dispatches integrate, collision resolution, and transition evaluation to the appropriate state structs. Interfaces IMinimalLocomotionSystem Marker interface for the Minimal locomotion system. IMinimalState Concrete intermediate interface — states implement this instead of the full generic interface. IMinimalTransition Concrete transition interface — hides the full generic type params. User implements: [LocomotionTransition(typeof(FromState), typeof(ToState))] struct MyTransition : IMinimalTransition Enums MinimalStates Identifies each state in the Minimal locomotion state machine.

api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.A.title: Class BaseCharacterLocomotorAuthoring<TProfile>.BaseCharacterLocomotorBaker<TAuthoring, TStateMachine, TStates, TContext, TInput, TStateData> | MGM Character Controller
api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.A.summary: Class BaseCharacterLocomotorAuthoring<TProfile>.BaseCharacterLocomotorBaker<TAuthoring, TStateMachine, TStates, TContext, TInput, TStateData> Baker for the CharacterAuthoring. Converts the authoring data into an ECS entity with the following setup: Creates the character entity with TransformUsageFlags.ManualOverride and manually adds LocalTransform and LocalToWorld built from the authoring Transform. The character is always produced as an unparented root entity — related entities (player, follower/model) link to it via explicit references, not via the ECS transform hierarchy or LinkedEntityGroup. If a CharacterProfile is provided: – Generates or reuses a BlobAssetReference from the profile asset (and calls DependsOn so changes re-bake automatically) – Adds LocomotionInput to drive character movement from player input or AI Agent – Builds a CapsuleCollider from profile settings (CapsuleGeometry + CollisionFilter) and adds it as a PhysicsCollider blob asset – Registers the character with the physics world (PhysicsWorldIndex) – Adds LocomotionProfileBlob (points to the blob asset), LocomotionVelocity, LocomotionContact, and LocomotionGravity (seeded from the default physics-step gravity) – Adds the state machine component left at its default state (enum value 0); api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.A.title: Class BaseCharacterLocomotorAuthoring<TProfile> | MGM Character Controller
api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.A.summary: Class BaseCharacterLocomotorAuthoring<TProfile> Serves as a base class for authoring character entities with locomotion capabilities. Designed to work with a profile of type TProfile, enabling customization of character movement and behavior through specific profile definitions. Contains shared properties and functionality for setting up entities related to character locomotion, including rendering models and defining state machines through further specialization. The class includes a nested abstract baker class used for converting authoring data into ECS entities with the following configurations: Associates the authored character with a profile asset (defining locomotion behavior and rules). Supports optional assignment of a prefab model entity for visual representation. Facilitates the integration of locomotion state machines, states, and custom contexts specific to the movement profile. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.R.summary: Struct CharacterPhysicsProfile Represents a physics configuration profile for a character, encapsulating core properties that define collision behavior, dimensions, and interaction with physics layers. Declaration public float CapsuleRadius Field Value Type Description float CollidesWith Collision layer the character capsule can collide with. Declaration public LayerMask CollidesWith Field Value Type Description LayerMask CollisionTolerance Skin thickness used for all collision queries. Defaults to Unity Physics' CollisionWorld tolerance. Declaration public float CollisionTolerance Field Value Type Description float CrushAngle Minimum angle between two opposing contact plane normals for the character to be considered crushed. When triggered, OverlapState.Crush is set and the locomotion pipeline skips its movement step that frame, freezing the character in place. Higher values (closer to 180°) mean tighter detection — only near-perfectly anti-parallel planes trigger Crush, leaving narrower wedges to resolve normally via the overlap solver. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.R.summary: Namespace WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Runtime.Components Structs CharacterFollower Registers an entity to follow a CharacterPath. CharacterPhysicsProfile Represents a physics configuration profile for a character, encapsulating core properties that define collision behavior, dimensions, and interaction with physics layers. CharacterPhysicsProfileBlob ECS component wrapping a blob asset reference to a baked CharacterPhysicsProfile. ControlledCharacters List of character entity controlled by the player or AI Agent FixedStepRate Singleton component that defines the physics fixed update timestep (in seconds). Baked from FixedStepRateAuthoring in a SubScene and applied at runtime by ApplyFixedStepRateSystem. Impact Describes a collision impact event between two physics bodies. LocomotionContact Last ground or obstacle contact for a Locomotor entity. LocomotionGravity Encapsulates gravity settings for the character. This value can be updated by a system to simulate any arbitrary gravity direction. LocomotionInputAsset<TInput> Stores a reference to the original PlayerInputAsset used by a player. LocomotionInputInstance<TInput> Stores a reference to the PlayerInputAsset<TInput> instance of a player. LocomotionProfileBlob<TProfile> Locomotion profile in the form of a blob asset. This profile contains configuration and parameters necessary for defining locomotion behavior within a state machine. LocomotionVelocity Locomotion velocity for a character locomotor. PhysicsBody Lightweight reference to a physics rigid body, pairing its index and entity. PlatformMover Component driving a platform entity along a predefined track at a given speed. PlayerCameraHandle Component storing a reference to the player camera's target transform. PlayerGameObjectInstance Set of references to mono objects. These are used to update and managed game object behaviors of the player entity from systems allowing for greater control on the player loop. PlayerGameObjectPrefab Set of references to mono objects. These are used to update and managed game object behaviors of the player entity from systems allowing for greater control on the player loop. PostCollisionImpulse Represents the impulse applied to a rigid body following a collision event. Rotor Component marking an entity as a rotating platform, providing its rotation axis. Track Buffer element defining one waypoint position on a platform track. Enums BodyType Classifies the physics body type of a collision contact surface. ContactType Classifies the geometry of the collision contact surface. InterpolationMode Controls whether the character's transform is updated via physics graphical smoothing interpolation.

api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.S.summary: Struct MuseumBotCaptureSystem Snapshots the pristine baked jump trigger of every character an exhibit streams in, before any tick can consume it. It runs in InitializationSystemGroup after SceneSystemGroup — the group that moves streamed-in section entities into the world — and Initialization precedes Simulation in the same frame, so the value captured is the one the baker wrote (MUS-9). The memory dies with its entity, so an exhibit streamed in again on the next lap is captured afresh (MUS-8). api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.S.title: Struct MuseumBotReArmSystem | MGM Character Controller
api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.S.summary: Struct MuseumBotReArmSystem Tops the jump trigger back up to its baked value once the character is grounded again, so a jump exhibit keeps jumping for its whole dwell (MUS-9). This is the museum's ONLY write into an exhibit. A character with nothing baked is never touched (MUS-10), and an unconsumed trigger is left alone rather than accumulated. ContactType.Ground is the same predicate the Idling/Moving transitions use, so the re-arm and the transition cannot disagree; the trigger cannot be eaten as a mid-air chained jump because the machine has already transitioned out of Jumping by the time this system reads the contact. OrderFirst is REQUIRED, not decorative: FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup is itself [UpdateInGroup(typeof(SimulationSystemGroup), OrderFirst = true)], and the sorter discards any ordering constraint that crosses the OrderFirst/middle/OrderLast partition boundary (with a warning, every Play session). Both systems must sit in the same partition for the UpdateBefore to be honoured — which is exactly how the generated input reader writes input ahead of the fixed step. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.S.summary: Class GeneratorSnapshotTests Snapshot tests for the state-machine source generator. The generator is run over the REAL sample sources shipped in the package (one compilation per sample, mirroring Unity's per-asmdef compilation), and every emitted file is compared byte-for-byte (after newline normalization) against a checked-in snapshot under Snapshots/. Any change to the generator that alters its output for currently-valid input fails these tests — additive work (e.g. new diagnostics) must keep them green. Baseline / deliberate re-baseline: set env MGMCC_SNAPSHOT_RECORD=1 and run dotnet test once; snapshots are (re)written. The generator is purely syntax-driven (no SemanticModel), so the sample sources are parsed without any metadata references; emission depends only on syntax. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.title: Class JumpOffMomentumTests | MGM Character Controller
api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class JumpOffMomentumTests PLT-7b — jump-off momentum on a dedicated, isolated Gym surface. Behaviour under test (from PLT-7b): a character riding a horizontally moving platform carries the platform's horizontal velocity into a jump. At the instant it leaves the surface its horizontal speed equals the platform's. Platform momentum is inherited automatically by the controller (Jumping.OnEnterState does HorizontalVelocity += PlatformHorizontalVelocity, exactly once); a game's jump logic must not add it a second time. If it were double-added the lift-off horizontal speed would be ~2x the platform speed — which this test rejects. ============================================================================================ SCENE CONTRACT for dev (plt7-author-scene) — subscene filename: "Jump_MovingPlatform" Resolution is by exact filename (see BehaviorTestsFixture.ResolveSceneGuid); the folder is dev's choice — recommended: Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Scenes/BehaviourTests/KinematicPlatform/Jump_MovingPlatform.unity (sibling of the KinematicPlatform scenes; shares the Jump_ prefix of Jump_FlatGround / Jump_OneWayPlatforms since the behaviour is a jump). This test is RED until that scene exists (ResolveSceneGuid fails loudly when the SceneAsset is absent). The scene must contain, isolated (one character, one platform), and self-contained: One KINEMATIC platform authored with MovingPlatformAuthoring (+ PlatformAuthoring + kinematic Rigidbody). Its Track is two waypoints laid out along +X so the platform translates in a straight line at a constant horizontal velocity through the whole run (make the leg long enough — e.g. 20 m — that it never reaches the far waypoint and reverses before lift-off). Authored Speed = 1 (m/s) — the MovingPlatformAuthoring default, matching the existing KinematicPlatform scenes (which author 1 / 10 / 100). Direction = world +X. => the character must inherit a horizontal velocity of ~(+1, 0) in the XZ plane at lift-off. One character bot (the SimpleCharacter prefab used by the other BehaviourTests scenes) resting on top of the platform, with SimpleCharacterBotAuthoring Move = (0,0,0) and Jump = true. Zero movement means the ONLY horizontal velocity the character can have at lift-off is what it inherits from the platform. The one-shot jump waits until the character is grounded (FromIdlingToJumping requires IsGroundingContact), so the bot settles onto and rides the moving platform before jumping — no ramp needed. Default -Y gravity, character upright (so "horizontal" == the XZ plane). If the scene depends on shared physics/ground config it may reuse World-SubScene (loaded in SetUp below); the character rides the elevated platform, so a shared floor does not interfere. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class MuseumBotDriverTests What the exhibits do while on display — MUS-9 (jump exhibits keep jumping) and MUS-10 (the museum adds nothing to the other exhibits). The gate entity is created here the way MuseumDirector creates it when the museum scene plays, so both systems are live. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Namespace WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Editor Namespaces WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Editor.Museum Classes ApiSurfaceTests CAM-2 public-surface guards for the 0.8.0 breaking removal of averaged multi-character camera framing. These are absence-of-symbol / ordinal-stability checks over the public FollowStrategy enum, written by reflection so the test compiles both BEFORE and AFTER dev deletes the trailing Average member (the member is never named as a compile-time symbol — only the enum TYPE is). See architecture §3.1 and ADR-6. BehaviorTests BehaviorTestsFixture CameraFramingTests CAM-1 verification pin — the multi-character camera frames the PRIMARY (first) controlled character; averaged multi-character framing is not offered anywhere. Per architecture §3.1 this behaviour is already hard-wired, independent of the (dead) FollowStrategy enum: BasePlayerCharacterAuthoring bakes CharacterFollower.FollowedEntity from the first controlled character, and CharacterFollowerSystem copies that single entity's transform onto the camera-target follower (which CameraRigFollowControlledCharacterSystem then applies to the camera rig). So this test is expected GREEN immediately — it is a regression pin that the removal of averaged framing left single-target framing intact, not a Red. Cheapest useful level: a headless in-test entity setup (no sample subscene, no physics) that mirrors how the follower is baked/populated, then one deterministic world tick that runs the production CharacterFollowerSystem in its real transform group. GoldenMasterTests Golden-master trajectory tests — the behavior-freeze instrument for refactoring safely. Each behavior scene is simulated for its canonical duration while every tick's observable state is hashed. The hash sequence is compared against a recorded snapshot in Tests/GoldenMasters/. Any refactor of the runtime must keep these bitwise-identical; intentional float-op reordering may be verified in tolerance mode after review. Usage: First run / deliberate re-baseline: set env MGMCC_GOLDEN_RECORD=1 and run the fixture — snapshots are (re)written and the tests pass with a "recorded" message. CI / refactor gate: run normally — missing snapshots are Inconclusive, mismatches fail with the first divergent tick and sample. Tolerance verification: set env MGMCC_GOLDEN_TOLERANCE=1 — compares the periodic full-state samples within 1e-5 instead of bitwise hashes. InputPipelineTests Input-pipeline characterization tests — exercise the generated input reader path: asset poll → NativeHashMap snapshot → ApplyInputsJob fan-out → ICharacterLocomotionInput accumulation on the character. The scripted asset below replaces the Input-System-backed PlayerInputAsset, so the tests drive the exact production systems with deterministic inputs and freeze the CURRENT semantics: Movement/IsSprinting/IsJumping are overwritten per read, JumpTrigger ACCUMULATES across reads until a consumer clears it (the mechanism that keeps Update-rate triggers alive for the next fixed tick — and, characterized here, also stacks multiple reads that happen before any consumption). JumpOffMomentumTests PLT-7b — jump-off momentum on a dedicated, isolated Gym surface. Behaviour under test (from PLT-7b): a character riding a horizontally moving platform carries the platform's horizontal velocity into a jump. At the instant it leaves the surface its horizontal speed equals the platform's. Platform momentum is inherited automatically by the controller (Jumping.OnEnterState does HorizontalVelocity += PlatformHorizontalVelocity, exactly once); a game's jump logic must not add it a second time. If it were double-added the lift-off horizontal speed would be ~2x the platform speed — which this test rejects. ============================================================================================ SCENE CONTRACT for dev (plt7-author-scene) — subscene filename: "Jump_MovingPlatform" Resolution is by exact filename (see BehaviorTestsFixture.ResolveSceneGuid); the folder is dev's choice — recommended: Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Scenes/BehaviourTests/KinematicPlatform/Jump_MovingPlatform.unity (sibling of the KinematicPlatform scenes; shares the Jump_ prefix of Jump_FlatGround / Jump_OneWayPlatforms since the behaviour is a jump). This test is RED until that scene exists (ResolveSceneGuid fails loudly when the SceneAsset is absent). The scene must contain, isolated (one character, one platform), and self-contained: One KINEMATIC platform authored with MovingPlatformAuthoring (+ PlatformAuthoring + kinematic Rigidbody). Its Track is two waypoints laid out along +X so the platform translates in a straight line at a constant horizontal velocity through the whole run (make the leg long enough — e.g. 20 m — that it never reaches the far waypoint and reverses before lift-off). Authored Speed = 1 (m/s) — the MovingPlatformAuthoring default, matching the existing KinematicPlatform scenes (which author 1 / 10 / 100). Direction = world +X. => the character must inherit a horizontal velocity of ~(+1, 0) in the XZ plane at lift-off. One character bot (the SimpleCharacter prefab used by the other BehaviourTests scenes) resting on top of the platform, with SimpleCharacterBotAuthoring Move = (0,0,0) and Jump = true. Zero movement means the ONLY horizontal velocity the character can have at lift-off is what it inherits from the platform. The one-shot jump waits until the character is grounded (FromIdlingToJumping requires IsGroundingContact), so the bot settles onto and rides the moving platform before jumping — no ramp needed. Default -Y gravity, character upright (so "horizontal" == the XZ plane). If the scene depends on shared physics/ground config it may reuse World-SubScene (loaded in SetUp below); the character rides the elevated platform, so a shared floor does not interfere. This is the pattern algorithm-branch tests build on: assemble a couple of primitives, issue the real cast, assert. StateSequenceTests State-machine characterization tests — assert WHICH state a character is in over time, covering the state-machine semantics the physics-outcome tests cannot see. Two layers: Semantic invariants — properties of the current behavior that must survive any behavior-preserving refactor (episode counts, terminal states, no flicker). Exact-sequence freeze — the full per-character (tick, state) transition log is recorded to Tests/GoldenMasters/<scene>.states.txt and compared exactly thereafter, using the same MGMCC_GOLDEN_RECORD=1 environment switch as the trajectory masters. The oracle is the CURRENT implementation: expected sequences are produced by running the code, reviewed for sanity, then frozen — not hand-derived from a spec. These recordings are the raw material for writing such a spec later.

api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class FrameBudgetTestBase PERF-4 (Mode B — architecture §3.2.2) shared body for the 30 000-character frame-budget gates that back (or refute) the "30 000 characters @ 60 fps" store claim (DOC-2). PERF-4 is split into two honest variants that share this base and differ ONLY in whether rendering is folded into the measured frame time: PERF-4a — simulation (SimulationFrameBudgetTests): runs headless (-nographics, forge default), so Measure.Frames times the CPU simulation loop with rendering EXCLUDED. This is the sub-claim number. PERF-4b — full loop (RenderFrameBudgetTests): runs with a real graphics device (-force-d3d11, via forge test … --graphics) and a runtime camera framing the population, so the measured frame time INCLUDES render + present. This is the number a customer reads as "30 000 @ 60 fps". Each variant SELF-GATES on the graphics device (RequiresGraphicsDevice vs SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType) and Assert.Ignore(string)s when the run is in the wrong mode — so one forge test --platform playmode asserts the sim number while the render test ignores, and one forge test --platform playmode --graphics asserts the render number while the sim test ignores. Neither variant is a real IL2CPP player build; even the -force-d3d11 offscreen render is closer-but-not-equal to a standalone Player (the truest number is a shipped build). Grounded AND moving precondition (director directive 2026-07-17). Before measuring, this base waits until the spawned population is at STEADY STATE: every character is grounded (Ground) AND at least MinMovingFraction of them are moving (planar speed > MinPlanarSpeed). Movement is BAKED into the BotCharacterPerf prefab (SimpleCharacterBotAuthoring.Move, seeded onto SimpleCharacterInput at bake time and carried through the spawner's Instantiate by the IncludePrefab query in SimpleCharacterBotBakingSystem), so the spawned population self-locomotes from the first tick with no runtime input write — the number reflects the real working scenario (active locomotion + physics + render), not an idle/settling transient. A failure to reach steady state inside the timeout fails loudly, so a stale/idle measurement can never be recorded. Claim linkage / clean-room canon (ADR-4). The median-≤-16.67 ms assertion is made ONLY on the clean-room reference machine (ReferenceMachineName, or forced via the ReferenceMachineEnvVar env var). On every OTHER machine the test still runs the full workload and logs the number, but replaces the assertion with an explicit Assert.Ignore(string). A breach on the reference machine REMOVES/relabels the marketing claim (DOC-2 re-spec, new PR) and never blocks the merge — PERF-4 gates the claim, not the merge. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class PerfSpawnerFixture Shared plumbing for the PERF-1…5 perf harness over the PerfSpawner surface (Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Scenes/PerfTests/PerfSpawner.unity). Loads the scene as a subscene, drives the non-interactive spawn seam, and ticks the world deterministically until the spawned population settles grounded. ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── SEAM CONTRACT for dev (implement EXACTLY this — shape from architecture §3.2.3 item 1): ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── New public component in the SHOWCASE spawner assembly (WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Runtime, file under Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Runtime/): namespace WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Runtime { public struct SpawnRequest : IComponentData { public int Count; } } Consumption in SpawningSystem (InitializationSystemGroup, inside m_world.Update()): when a SpawnRequest exists, spawn EXACTLY Count characters of the spawner prefab in the deterministic Grid layout (ADR-5: Grid is the locked perf pattern), then CONSUME the request (remove the component / destroy the request entity) so it fires once. Grid derivation from N (per §3.3): columns = ceil(sqrt(Count)); rows = ceil(Count / columns); spawn exactly Count entities (last row partial — NOT columns*rows rounded up), using the AUTHORED GridSpacing, centered on the spawner origin (LocalToWorld.Position). The interactive Enter-key path and this seam MUST share ONE spawn implementation (redraw the boundary so the spawn trigger is not welded to input). Headless input guard (blocks this fixture TODAY): SpawningSystem.OnUpdate dereferences Keyboard.current/Mouse.current unconditionally. In batchmode / a headless test world these are null, so the very first world Update (during LoadSubScenes) NREs before the seam is ever reached. Guard every Keyboard.current/Mouse.current access with a null check. The SpawnRequest seam (items 1–3 above) is now IMPLEMENTED, so this assembly compiles and the fast N=100 correctness case is green. The remaining Red lives in the behaviour, not the compile: the 30 000-capacity case (PERF-1) and the per-tier zero-alloc gate (PERF-5) are the signals that fail if the sim can't scale or allocates on the tick. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class SimulationFrequencyMatrixTests Sim-rate × population cost matrix (EditMode, characterization — NOT a gate). Sweeps the character count {1, 100, 1000, 10000, 20000, 30000} against the simulation frequency {20, 30, 50, 60} Hz and records, for each cell, the cost of ONE 60-fps-cadence simulation-path frame at that rate and population. It answers "how does the per-frame simulation cost scale with sim frequency and crowd size?" — the question behind the 30 000 @ 60 fps claim once the sim runs at a real 60 Hz. Metric per cell — sim-path ms per 60 fps frame (render EXCLUDED). Each measured frame advances a fixed 1/60 s of world time (the 60-fps render cadence) and runs only the simulation path (AdvanceOneSimulationPathTick() = Initialization + Simulation groups, no presentation/render). At sim rate F the FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup runs F/60 fixed ticks per frame (physics + locomotor over the whole population), so the cell cost rises with F. The figure is directly comparable to the 16.67 ms 60-fps budget (the simulation share of it). Because rendering is not capped in the shipped scenario, a frame rendered faster than 60 fps carries fewer than F/60 ticks and costs less — the 60-fps cadence here is the reference the claim is stated at. Efficiency: the expensive spawn+settle is paid ONCE per count and reused across all four frequencies (the sim rate is re-applied between measurements via the FixedStepRate singleton, which ApplyFixedStepRateSystem pushes onto the group each frame). Mean is the headline (it averages the fixed-tick beat over frames); median is logged alongside. This suite does not assert a budget — it records the surface for the director / DOC-2. The only hard precondition is that the population settles grounded, so a still-falling measurement can never be recorded. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Class SimulationMemoryTests Simulation-path MEMORY ALLOCATION measurement (EditMode). MEASURES ONLY — it does not gate. For each character count {1, 100, 1000, 10000, 20000, 30000} it spawns and settles the population, then measures the managed heap bytes allocated per simulation-path tick (physics + locomotor, presentation excluded) and records it as a SimAllocBytes_{n} sample group in bytes per tick. Counterpart to SimulationFrequencyMatrixTests (which measures the TIME cost surface): that suite answers "how fast is a frame", this one answers "how much does the sim path allocate". Neither asserts a budget — they are characterization surfaces for the perf report, not pass/fail gates. The one hard precondition here is the same as everywhere in this fixture: the population must settle grounded, so a still-falling measurement can never be recorded. Method — byte-exact, no instrumentation in the counter span. Allocation is measured with GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread() (thread-local, so a background editor task on another thread cannot pollute it) captured AROUND a raw window of WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Performance.SimulationMemoryTests.AllocWindowTicks sim-path ticks — no Measure.* instrumentation inside the window, whose own per-iteration bookkeeping would otherwise be counted as sim allocation. Two windows are sampled and the larger reported, so a deterministic per-tick allocation (which repeats in both) is never under-reported. A managed allocation on the sim main thread shows up here as a non-zero B/tick figure; a Burst-clean sim path reads 0. api/WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.T.summary: Namespace WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Performance Classes FrameBudgetTestBase PERF-4 (Mode B — architecture §3.2.2) shared body for the 30 000-character frame-budget gates that back (or refute) the "30 000 characters @ 60 fps" store claim (DOC-2). PERF-4 is split into two honest variants that share this base and differ ONLY in whether rendering is folded into the measured frame time: PERF-4a — simulation (SimulationFrameBudgetTests): runs headless (-nographics, forge default), so Measure.Frames times the CPU simulation loop with rendering EXCLUDED. This is the sub-claim number. PERF-4b — full loop (RenderFrameBudgetTests): runs with a real graphics device (-force-d3d11, via forge test … --graphics) and a runtime camera framing the population, so the measured frame time INCLUDES render + present. This is the number a customer reads as "30 000 @ 60 fps". Each variant SELF-GATES on the graphics device (RequiresGraphicsDevice vs SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType) and Assert.Ignore(string)s when the run is in the wrong mode — so one forge test --platform playmode asserts the sim number while the render test ignores, and one forge test --platform playmode --graphics asserts the render number while the sim test ignores. Neither variant is a real IL2CPP player build; even the -force-d3d11 offscreen render is closer-but-not-equal to a standalone Player (the truest number is a shipped build). Grounded AND moving precondition (director directive 2026-07-17). Before measuring, this base waits until the spawned population is at STEADY STATE: every character is grounded (Ground) AND at least MinMovingFraction of them are moving (planar speed > MinPlanarSpeed). Movement is BAKED into the BotCharacterPerf prefab (SimpleCharacterBotAuthoring.Move, seeded onto SimpleCharacterInput at bake time and carried through the spawner's Instantiate by the IncludePrefab query in SimpleCharacterBotBakingSystem), so the spawned population self-locomotes from the first tick with no runtime input write — the number reflects the real working scenario (active locomotion + physics + render), not an idle/settling transient. A failure to reach steady state inside the timeout fails loudly, so a stale/idle measurement can never be recorded. Claim linkage / clean-room canon (ADR-4). The median-≤-16.67 ms assertion is made ONLY on the clean-room reference machine (ReferenceMachineName, or forced via the ReferenceMachineEnvVar env var). On every OTHER machine the test still runs the full workload and logs the number, but replaces the assertion with an explicit Assert.Ignore(string). A breach on the reference machine REMOVES/relabels the marketing claim (DOC-2 re-spec, new PR) and never blocks the merge — PERF-4 gates the claim, not the merge. PerfSpawnerFixture Shared plumbing for the PERF-1…5 perf harness over the PerfSpawner surface (Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Scenes/PerfTests/PerfSpawner.unity). Loads the scene as a subscene, drives the non-interactive spawn seam, and ticks the world deterministically until the spawned population settles grounded. ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── SEAM CONTRACT for dev (implement EXACTLY this — shape from architecture §3.2.3 item 1): ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── New public component in the SHOWCASE spawner assembly (WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Runtime, file under Samples/BehaviorShowCase/Runtime/): namespace WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Runtime { public struct SpawnRequest : IComponentData { public int Count; } } Consumption in SpawningSystem (InitializationSystemGroup, inside m_world.Update()): when a SpawnRequest exists, spawn EXACTLY Count characters of the spawner prefab in the deterministic Grid layout (ADR-5: Grid is the locked perf pattern), then CONSUME the request (remove the component / destroy the request entity) so it fires once. Grid derivation from N (per §3.3): columns = ceil(sqrt(Count)); rows = ceil(Count / columns); spawn exactly Count entities (last row partial — NOT columns*rows rounded up), using the AUTHORED GridSpacing, centered on the spawner origin (LocalToWorld.Position). The interactive Enter-key path and this seam MUST share ONE spawn implementation (redraw the boundary so the spawn trigger is not welded to input). Headless input guard (blocks this fixture TODAY): SpawningSystem.OnUpdate dereferences Keyboard.current/Mouse.current unconditionally. In batchmode / a headless test world these are null, so the very first world Update (during LoadSubScenes) NREs before the seam is ever reached. Guard every Keyboard.current/Mouse.current access with a null check. The SpawnRequest seam (items 1–3 above) is now IMPLEMENTED, so this assembly compiles and the fast N=100 correctness case is green. The remaining Red lives in the behaviour, not the compile: the 30 000-capacity case (PERF-1) and the per-tier zero-alloc gate (PERF-5) are the signals that fail if the sim can't scale or allocates on the tick. RenderFrameBudgetTests PERF-4b — the 30 000-character FULL-LOOP frame budget (rendering INCLUDED). Runs with a real graphics device under -force-d3d11 (run with forge test --platform playmode --graphics) and creates a runtime camera + light framing the population, so Measure.Frames times the full player loop: simulation PLUS the character render path PLUS present. This is the number a customer reads as "30 000 @ 60 fps" — it is the one PERF-4 must be adjudicated on. The BotCharacterPerf render path is Entity Graphics: a baked MeshRenderer becomes RenderMeshArray + MaterialMeshInfo drawn by the pure-ECS instanced batch renderer (no per-character companion GameObject), so the render cost at 30k is the EG cull/batch/submit + present cost; that is the honest point. Self-gates via RequiresGraphicsDevice = true: under the headless -nographics default this test Assert.Ignores (a headless run cannot measure render), so run it explicitly with --graphics. Even -force-d3d11 offscreen render is closer-but-not-equal to a real IL2CPP Player build — the truest number is a standalone build. The median-≤-16.67 ms assertion is made on the clean-room reference machine only (ADR-4). SimulationFrameBudgetTests PERF-4a — the 30 000-character SIMULATION frame budget (rendering EXCLUDED). Runs headless under -nographics (the forge default; run with forge test --platform playmode), so Measure.Frames times the CPU simulation loop only — no GPU, no present. This is the honest simulation sub-claim: what the character-controller sim costs per frame at 30k, NOT a rendered fps. For the full-loop number a customer reads as "30 000 @ 60 fps", see RenderFrameBudgetTests (PERF-4b, --graphics). Self-gates via RequiresGraphicsDevice = false: if a real graphics device is present (a --graphics run) this test Assert.Ignores so render work is never folded into the sim number. The full workload (spawn 30k, grounded+moving steady state, measure) still runs; the median-≤-16.67 ms assertion is made on the clean-room reference machine only (ADR-4). SimulationFrequencyMatrixTests Sim-rate × population cost matrix (EditMode, characterization — NOT a gate). Sweeps the character count {1, 100, 1000, 10000, 20000, 30000} against the simulation frequency {20, 30, 50, 60} Hz and records, for each cell, the cost of ONE 60-fps-cadence simulation-path frame at that rate and population. It answers "how does the per-frame simulation cost scale with sim frequency and crowd size?" — the question behind the 30 000 @ 60 fps claim once the sim runs at a real 60 Hz. Metric per cell — sim-path ms per 60 fps frame (render EXCLUDED). Each measured frame advances a fixed 1/60 s of world time (the 60-fps render cadence) and runs only the simulation path (AdvanceOneSimulationPathTick() = Initialization + Simulation groups, no presentation/render). At sim rate F the FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup runs F/60 fixed ticks per frame (physics + locomotor over the whole population), so the cell cost rises with F. The figure is directly comparable to the 16.67 ms 60-fps budget (the simulation share of it). Because rendering is not capped in the shipped scenario, a frame rendered faster than 60 fps carries fewer than F/60 ticks and costs less — the 60-fps cadence here is the reference the claim is stated at. Efficiency: the expensive spawn+settle is paid ONCE per count and reused across all four frequencies (the sim rate is re-applied between measurements via the FixedStepRate singleton, which ApplyFixedStepRateSystem pushes onto the group each frame). Mean is the headline (it averages the fixed-tick beat over frames); median is logged alongside. This suite does not assert a budget — it records the surface for the director / DOC-2. The only hard precondition is that the population settles grounded, so a still-falling measurement can never be recorded. SimulationMemoryTests Simulation-path MEMORY ALLOCATION measurement (EditMode). MEASURES ONLY — it does not gate. For each character count {1, 100, 1000, 10000, 20000, 30000} it spawns and settles the population, then measures the managed heap bytes allocated per simulation-path tick (physics + locomotor, presentation excluded) and records it as a SimAllocBytes_{n} sample group in bytes per tick. Counterpart to SimulationFrequencyMatrixTests (which measures the TIME cost surface): that suite answers "how fast is a frame", this one answers "how much does the sim path allocate". Neither asserts a budget — they are characterization surfaces for the perf report, not pass/fail gates. The one hard precondition here is the same as everywhere in this fixture: the population must settle grounded, so a still-falling measurement can never be recorded. Method — byte-exact, no instrumentation in the counter span. Allocation is measured with GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread() (thread-local, so a background editor task on another thread cannot pollute it) captured AROUND a raw window of WAYN.Games.MGM.CharacterController.Tests.Performance.SimulationMemoryTests.AllocWindowTicks sim-path ticks — no Measure.* instrumentation inside the window, whose own per-iteration bookkeeping would otherwise be counted as sim allocation. Two windows are sampled and the larger reported, so a deterministic per-tick allocation (which repeats in both) is never under-reported. A managed allocation on the sim main thread shows up here as a non-zero B/tick figure; a Burst-clean sim path reads 0. SpawnCapacityTests PERF-1 correctness precondition: request N via the non-interactive spawn seam, settle, then assert exactly N characters exist, each in ground contact, none below the floor. This is the spawn-count/settle setup that the PERF-2…5 measurements later reuse over the same PerfSpawner surface (architecture §3.2.3, §4 PERF-1 row). Two tiers are pinned here: the fast N = 100 tier and the capacity-raise N = 30 000 tier (perf-raise-scene-capacity-30k / perf-verify-30k-settles-grounded). Both assert the identical invariant via AssertExactlyGroundedNoneBelowFloor(int, bool, int, float).
